known_failures.detail: PATCH /api/providers returns 409 instead of 200 when it follows a job that just reported a terminal status: Worker clears active_identity in its finally block after publishing the status, so queue_busy() still sees a busy worker. Same race as the two entries below. Reproduced on fa7a46d without the B2 changes (2 failures in 3 runs), so it predates them.
POST /api/extensions/{id}/disable returns 409 for the same worker race: the job reports succeeded before active_identity is cleared.
POST /api/extensions/redis-runtime/disable returns 409 for the same worker race: the job reports succeeded before active_identity is cleared.

tasks.title: User store and password policy

tasks.acceptance: Tests cover hashing, role checks, weak password refusal, duplicate user refusal.
tasks.note: passwords.py stores Argon2id (m=19456,t=2,p=1) and still verifies legacy pbkdf2 with an in-place upgrade on login; users.py owns roles admin/operator/viewer, case-insensitive unique lowercase usernames, the 12-512 character policy (blocklist, username containment, 4 distinct characters, no composition rule), last-administrator protection, and rotation that revokes sessions and retires the matching plaintext line from bootstrap-credentials.txt (file deleted when empty). Human-only endpoints GET/POST /api/users, PATCH /api/users/{id}, POST /api/users/{id}/password, never exposed to agent scopes; docs/USERS.md plus README, AGENT_ACCESS, IMPLEMENTATION and CHANGELOG updates; 24 tests cover hashing, legacy upgrade, every refusal reason, duplicate and invalid accounts, role checks, last-admin, self/admin rotation, bootstrap retirement and agent denial

tasks.title: Session security
tasks.detail: Replace the ad-hoc session with httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies, absolute and idle timeouts, CSRF token bound to the session, logout invalidation, rate limited login.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover cookie flags, expiry, CSRF mismatch, brute-force throttling.
tasks.note: sessions.py owns the kw_session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, Secure over HTTPS, Max-Age 28800) and hashed tokens of the form <issued-at>.<secret>, so the 8h absolute deadline is derived from the token and survives restarts without a schema change; sessions.expires is the 30 min idle deadline, pushed forward only inside its last minute and capped at the absolute deadline, expired rows are deleted when presented and the stale cookie is cleared with Max-Age=0. login_throttle.py adds two 60s sliding windows (10 failures per client and account, 30 per client), answered with 429 and Retry-After before the password is checked, unknown accounts counted like wrong passwords, bounded to 1024 keys and cleared per pair on success. Login replaces any presented cookie (fixation), logout deletes the row and clears the cookie, rotation reuses the same service. CSRF stays bound to the session and the middleware now resolves sessions only for /api paths so /readyz still reports a dead database. docs/SESSIONS.md plus README, USERS, IMPLEMENTATION and CHANGELOG updates; 15 new tests cover cookie flags over HTTP and HTTPS, invalid credentials issuing no cookie, idle expiry with row deletion and cookie clearing, the absolute deadline on an otherwise live token, sliding refresh, activity never extending the absolute cap, CSRF absence/mismatch/cross-session reuse, logout replay, session fixation, brute-force and unknown-account throttling, bounded limiter memory, hashed storage, legacy token refusal and restart survival; suite 1422 passed, 2 skipped, with the three known queue_busy races

tasks.title: API tokens for agents
tasks.detail: Scope-limited tokens with expiry, rotation and revocation, audit entry per use, read-only scope still enforced for infrastructure reads.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover expiry, revocation, scope denial and audit records.
tasks.note: The prototype already stored tokens as SHA-256 digests with role-capped scopes, an absolute expiry, idempotent revocation, a closed required_scope map and human-admin-only management; this iteration added the two missing pieces. POST /api/agent-tokens/{id}/rotate replaces the secret in place, keeps id/label/role/scopes/created_at and the original expires_at so rotation cannot renew, invalidates the previous secret at once, answers 409 for revoked or expired tokens and 404 for unknown ids, requires a human admin session with CSRF and records agent_token.rotated. The middleware writes one agent.request row per authenticated machine request (actor agent:<id>, resource the token id, detail method/path/status/scope, never the credential); scope denials keep writing agent.request_denied and are not counted as uses; only the agent.request tail is bounded (newest 50000, pruned at most hourly, clock injectable) so issue/rotate/revoke/denial evidence is never pruned, and the retention DELETE is covered by the PostgreSQL translation test. docs/AGENT_ACCESS.md documents rotation, the audit trail and the retention, with README, IMPLEMENTATION and CHANGELOG updates. 6 new tests cover rotation in place, refusals (revoked, expired, unknown, viewer/operator, agent token, missing CSRF), per-use audit and denial separation, retention with decisions preserved, and a read:infrastructure token reading infrastructure while every write and unrelated read stays 403; suite 1430 passed, 2 skipped, 1 known queue_busy race. Frontend AgentAccess.tsx still exposes only issue and revoke.

tasks.title: OIDC-ready authentication
tasks.detail: Add a provider abstraction so an external identity provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Entra) can be configured without touching the login path; disabled by default.
tasks.acceptance: Tests cover disabled provider, discovery failure, and successful claim mapping with a stub.
tasks.note: oidc.py owns the optional provider: KUBERWEAVER_OIDC_ISSUER enables it, a partial or invalid configuration is reported as configuration_error without breaking password login, and discovery/JWKS are cached for 300s. GET /api/auth/oidc/start stores a single-use attempt (10 min, 1024 entries) with nonce and S256 PKCE, sets a SameSite=Lax kw_oidc state cookie and redirects; the callback requires that cookie to match state (login CSRF), exchanges the code with client_secret_post, verifies JWKS signature with an allowlisted algorithm, iss/aud/exp/iat, nonce and at_hash, then signs in only an existing local account: unknown accounts and accounts already bound to another subject are refused, first sign-in binds (issuer,sub) with a SHA-256 id, and the local role stays authoritative. New idempotent table oidc_identities registered in the PostgreSQL DDL translator; PyJWT pinned in requirements. docs/OIDC.md plus README, CONFIGURATION, IMPLEMENTATION and CHANGELOG updates. 14 tests cover the disabled default with working password login, incomplete configuration, discovery failure and issuer mismatch, full claim mapping with a stub (PKCE params, state cookie flags, binding, subject-wins over a renamed claim), unknown and already-linked accounts, state replay and cross-browser callback refusal, wrong nonce/audience/expiry/unsigned/foreign-key tokens, access-token hash, token endpoint refusal and no audit row for random states; suite 1445 passed, 2 skipped on the first full run; a second full run reproduced the recorded queue_busy race in test_provider_bindings (1444 passed, 1 known failure), unchanged from earlier iterations. Frontend login page not touched (API-only iteration).

tasks.title: Black and light theme
tasks.detail: CSS variables for both themes, persisted preference, no flash of wrong theme, no remote fonts.
tasks.acceptance: Frontend tests cover preference persistence and default; build passes.
tasks.note: style.css opens with one 60-token layer: black values in :root, which is the default, and light overrides under :root[data-theme=light]; every other rule reads var() and theme.test.ts refuses a colour literal outside the two blocks, a token missing from either theme, a token read but never defined, and any remote font (@import, font CDN, url(https). public/theme-boot.js applies kuberweaver.theme from <head> before the app module, as a classic script because the origin sends script-src 'self' and refuses inline code; index.html carries data-theme=dark plus the matching theme-color, and the test evaluates the boot script for unset, light, unknown and throwing storage and compares its key and both colours with theme.ts. useTheme keeps the document in step when it mounts without the boot script, follows storage events from another tab, and survives a refused write. The toggle (name 'Black theme', aria-pressed carries the state) sits in the top bar and on the login card. The light palette was consolidated into surfaces, text, borders and status scales; muted, faint, ghost and the four status texts were darkened so body text clears 4.5:1 and captions 3.5:1. Both themes were measured in headless Chromium: black shows no light surface at all, light keeps only the intended dark chrome (sidebar, primary button, console), and the faintest text is a decorative separator at 4.08 and 3.45; all body text and badges measure 4.5 or more. docs/THEMING.md, CHANGELOG and IMPLEMENTATION updated. Frontend 279 tests, tsc and build green; backend 1445 passed, 2 skipped.
